description: Passive quartz crystal unit (resonator): a two-terminal electromechanical resonator with no supply, output, or logic. Covers AT-cut MHz crystals (fundamental and overtone) and Y-cut / flexural 32.768 kHz tuning-fork crystals, in SMD and through-hole (HC-49) packages. The active clock sources that CONTAIN a crystal - XO / TCXO / VCXO / OCXO oscillators - are a separate family (supply, output driver, jitter, phase noise, pullability); do not fold their parameters here. Synthesized from a 20-datasheet corpus across Abracon, Epson, NDK, Kyocera, Citizen, TXC, Pletronics, QST, and Micro Crystal.

parameters.name: Nominal frequency
parameters.hint: The specified resonant frequency in Hz, base-SI with no SI prefix (32.768 kHz is 32768; 16 MHz is 1.6e7; 32.768 kHz tuning forks are exactly 32768). A datasheet 'frequency range' (e.g. 8-54 MHz) is the family's ordering axis, not a single part's tolerance - one emitted document pins one ordered frequency. Whether the value is the series- or parallel-resonant frequency depends on the RESONANCE condition; parallel-resonant frequency is specified at the stated load_capacitance.

parameters.name: Frequency tolerance
parameters.hint: The initial frequency deviation from nominal at the +25 C reference (typically +/-25 C +/-3 C), in ppm, NOT including aging or temperature drift. Store the symmetric magnitude (a +/-20 ppm part is 20; asymmetric bounds go in min/max). A tolerance printed in percent converts to ppm (x1e4: +/-0.003 % is +/-30 ppm). Measured at the specified load_capacitance and drive_level - attach both as conditions. The many tolerance grades a datasheet lists (+/-10 / +/-20 / +/-30 / +/-50) are ordering-selectable; one document pins one grade.

parameters.name: Frequency stability over temperature
aliases: frequency tolerance over operating temperature range
parameters.hint: The total frequency excursion, referenced to +25 C, across the whole operating temperature range - in ppm. This is a single band over a RANGE, NOT a per-degree slope: keep unit ppm and carry the temperature range as a T_A condition (or in conditionsVerbatim), never normalize it to ppm/degC. AT-cut MHz parts publish this directly (+/-30 ppm over -20..+70 C); 32.768 kHz tuning-fork parts instead publish parabolic_coefficient + turnover_temperature, from which the excursion is computed, and often omit this key. A low-cost sheet that prints a single 'inclusive' or 'overall' figure combining initial tolerance AND temperature drift maps here, with the merged basis noted in conditionsVerbatim.

parameters.name: Parabolic (turnover) temperature coefficient
parameters.hint: The second-order (parabolic) temperature coefficient of a tuning-fork / Y-cut crystal, in ppm per degree-Celsius-squared. The frequency-vs-temperature curve is a downward parabola about the turnover_temperature: Df/f = parabolic_coefficient * (T - turnover_temperature)^2. Universally about -0.035 to -0.04 ppm/degC2 for 32.768 kHz tuning forks; it is the defining thermal spec of that cut and cannot be derived from ppm/degC. Store the magnitude with its sign as printed (it is negative). Does not apply to AT-cut MHz parts, which use frequency_stability instead.

parameters.name: Turnover temperature
parameters.hint: The temperature at which a tuning-fork crystal's frequency-vs-temperature parabola reaches its apex (df/dT = 0), in degC - typically +25 C +/-5 C. Pairs with parabolic_coefficient to fully define the f-vs-T curve. Store as a point (with tolerance in min/max if printed as a range).

parameters.name: Operating temperature range
parameters.hint: The temperature range over which the electrical specs (tolerance, stability, ESR) are guaranteed, in degC. Store min = low bound, max = high bound. Automotive grades widen it to -40..+125 (Grade 1) or -40..+150 (Grade 0); each grade is a separate ordered part.

parameters.name: Storage temperature range
parameters.hint: The non-operating storage temperature range in degC (an absolute-maximum limit - set limitClass absolute_max). Store min/max bounds.

parameters.name: Equivalent series resistance
parameters.hint: The motional-arm resistance R1 at series resonance, in ohms (kOhm for 32.768 kHz tuning forks, ohms for MHz parts - normalize: 70 kOhm is 70000). ESR is SINGLE-valued for one ordered grade: a datasheet's ESR-limit-per-frequency-band table is a FAMILY ordering artifact across MPNs (each frequency is a different orderable part), and a wider-temperature part with a higher ESR limit is likewise a different grade - since one document is one grade (spec section 4), emit only the single value for that part's frequency and temperature range, never fold sibling grades' rows into an array. `array: true` with `conditionAxis: F` exists only for the deliberate case of a consumer emitting one multi-frequency family document. Measured at a stated drive level (attach DL) with a named fixture (IEC pi-network, network analyzer) in conditionsVerbatim. Vendor 'CI' = crystal impedance = ESR; 'Re' = effective series resistance.

parameters.name: Load capacitance
parameters.hint: The external load capacitance the parallel-resonant frequency is specified against, in farads (pF normalized: 12.5 pF is 12.5e-12). Ordering-selectable (common: 6/7/9/12.5/18 pF); one document pins one value. A SERIES-resonant part (vendor 'series' / 'S' option / CL printed as infinity) has NO load capacitance - OMIT this parameter entirely rather than storing a sentinel, and record RESONANCE = series.

parameters.name: Shunt (static) capacitance
parameters.hint: The static parallel-plate capacitance C0 of the electrodes and holder, in farads (pF normalized: ~1 pF for tuning forks, ~2-5 pF for MHz parts). Part of the equivalent circuit; with motional_capacitance sets the capacitance ratio C0/C1.

parameters.name: Motional capacitance
parameters.hint: The motional-arm capacitance C1 of the equivalent circuit, in farads (fF normalized: 3.4 fF is 3.4e-15). Seldom printed on commercial MHz sheets (derivable), but characteristic on tuning-fork parts. With shunt_capacitance it sets the capacitance_ratio C0/C1, and with ESR and nominal_frequency it determines quality_factor Q = 1/(2*pi*f0*C1*R1); store Q and the ratio directly when a datasheet prints them as guaranteed rows (see quality_factor, capacitance_ratio) rather than forcing the consumer to recompute.

parameters.name: Motional inductance
parameters.hint: The motional-arm inductance L1 of the equivalent circuit, in henries (mH..kH range; a tuning fork is thousands of henries). Rarely tabulated - it appears mainly in a SPICE / equivalent-circuit block. Derivable from motional_capacitance and nominal_frequency (L1 = 1/((2*pi*f0)^2 * C1)).

parameters.name: Quality factor
parameters.hint: The resonator's unloaded quality factor Q - a pure dimensionless number (unit `1`), typically 1e4 to 1e6 (tens of thousands for a 32.768 kHz tuning fork, hundreds of thousands to millions for precision parts). Q = 1/(2*pi*f0*C1*R1), so it is derivable from motional_capacitance, ESR, and nominal_frequency; store it here ONLY when a datasheet prints Q as a guaranteed spec row (some tuning-fork and precision/RF parts do), preserving the printed value rather than dropping it. Higher Q means sharper selectivity and lower phase noise in the oscillator that uses it.

parameters.name: Capacitance ratio
parameters.hint: The ratio of shunt to motional capacitance, C0/C1 - a pure dimensionless number (unit `1`), typically ~200-500. It is the master parameter that sets a crystal's pullability (the achievable Fs-to-Fa frequency span narrows as the ratio rises). Derivable from shunt_capacitance / motional_capacitance, but store it here when a datasheet prints it directly (many tuning-fork and precision sheets give a guaranteed max ratio without printing both capacitances).

parameters.name: Drive level
parameters.hint: The power dissipated in the crystal, in watts (uW normalized: 100 uW is 1e-4, 0.5 uW is 5e-7). Two senses distinguished by limitClass, NOT by separate keys: the recommended operating drive level (limitClass recommended, ~0.1-10 uW, at which ESR/tolerance are measured) and the maximum drive the part survives undamaged (limitClass absolute_max, 'GL' / 'maximum level of drive'). Excessive drive accelerates aging and can fracture a tuning fork.

parameters.name: Drive level dependency
parameters.hint: The change in frequency (ppm) or in ESR (%) as drive level is swept across the specified range (e.g. 1 uW to 500 uW, max-min). A DLD spec bounds how much the resonator's behavior moves with excitation; a large DLD indicates a defective or contaminated crystal. Store the frequency-shift figure in ppm, the ESR-shift figure in % (altUnit). Uncommon on commercial sheets.

parameters.name: Insulation resistance
parameters.hint: The DC resistance between terminals (and terminal-to-cover), in ohms (MOhm normalized: 500 MOhm is 5e8), measured at a stated DC bias (typically 100 Vdc). A minimum bound; attach the bias voltage as a V_DC condition.

parameters.name: Frequency aging
parameters.hint: The irreversible frequency change over a stated time window at constant temperature, in ppm - almost always given as a first-year bound (+/-3 ppm max, first year). Crystal aging is logarithmic, not linear, so this is NOT a per-year rate: keep unit ppm and carry the time window as an AGING_PERIOD condition (first_year, 10_year) - do NOT invent a ppm/year unit. A part specifying multiple horizons emits one measurement per horizon.

parameters.name: Frequency shift after environmental stress
parameters.hint: The permitted permanent frequency shift after a reliability stress (solder reflow, mechanical shock, vibration, thermal shock, moisture, board bending), in ppm. Usually one bound (+/-20 ppm) covers a whole environmental-test suite; carry the specific stress as a note-only TEST condition and the full setup (drop height, vibration sweep, reflow profile) in conditionsVerbatim - the mechanical setup never enters the unit enum. Often paired with an allowed ESR/CI change (store that as a separate equivalent_series_resistance measurement or in %).

parameters.name: Spurious response
parameters.hint: Attenuation of unwanted (spurious) resonance modes relative to the main mode, in dB (a minimum suppression). Specified mainly on RF and overtone crystals where a spurious mode near the wanted frequency can pull an oscillator. Store the suppression magnitude; the offset frequency of the spur goes in conditionsVerbatim.
